content:
This is a playful reference to the beloved children's book "If You Give a Mouse a Cookie" by Laura Joffe Numeroff! 

In the story, giving a mouse a cookie sets off a chain reaction of requests - the mouse will want milk to go with it, then a napkin to clean up, then a mirror to check for a milk mustache, and so on. Each favor leads to another request in an endless cycle.

The book is often used as a humorous metaphor for how small actions can lead to escalating consequences or how one favor can snowball into many more demands. Parents sometimes joke about it when talking about giving in to children's requests!

Of course, in real life, the main reason not to give an actual mouse a cookie would be more practical - cookies aren't healthy for mice, and you generally don't want to encourage mice to stick around your house by feeding them!
